01.n: The Hebrew has 'for the interest', with the article, but the sense is general. Gesenius cites this verse for the noun: interest, usury. It stands first for emphasis, as does 'increase' in the next clause.

03.r: To hand over silver as a loan.
03.n: The imperfect here describes what the righteous man habitually does, in a list that runs through these verses. The older translations put it in the past, 'hath not given forth'.

04.r: A second kind of gain from a loan.
04.n: Gesenius: from the root רָבָה, interest, usury, and he cites this verse. The same pair, interest and increase, appears in Leviticus 25:36 on this page. The BSB's 'excess interest' is an interpretation; the lexicons in the brief do not draw that line.

06.r: To take payment from the borrower.

07.n: The brief's lexicon and BDB give injustice, unrighteousness.

08.r: He keeps his hand away from wrongdoing.
08.n: The causative form of the ordinary verb 'to turn back, return': 'make (his hand) turn back'.

09.r: His hand, standing for what he does.

10.r: A just decision when two men are in dispute.
10.n: Gesenius gives first judgment, the act of judging. The phrase is literally 'judgment of truth'; Hebrew often uses a noun after another where English uses an adjective.

11.r: A judgment that holds firm and can be relied on.
11.n: The noun means firmness, faithfulness, truth; Gesenius puts firmness, stability first.

12.r: He gives a fair decision himself.

13.r: Between the two parties to a dispute.

15.n: Literally 'between a man and to a man': Hebrew says 'between X and to Y', so the small 'to' here is English 'and'.

_extra.0: καὶ (and): begins a phrase added by the Greek translators, 'and his silver'.
_extra.1: τὸ (the): part of the added phrase.
_extra.2: ἀργύριον (silver): the Greek supplies the object, 'his silver he will not give for interest'.
_extra.3: αὐτοῦ (his): part of the added phrase.
_extra.12: καὶ (and): added by the Greek translators.

03.n: The Greek uses the future, 'he will not give'.

04.n: πλεονασμός, an increase, a surplus, as in Leviticus 25:37 on this page.

07.n: ἀδικία, injustice. The first word, ἐξ ('from'), has no dictionary form in our data; it is ἐκ.

11.n: δίκαιος, just, righteous: the Greek says 'a just judgment' where the Hebrew says 'true'.

13.n: ἀνὰ μέσον, 'in the middle of', the Greek idiom for 'between'.

15.n: The Greek reads 'and between his neighbour', where the Hebrew says simply 'and man'.
